segments.text: Yashwada Nazar, this former IPS officer who joins me live.
We also have OP Rawat, former CEC.
Sanju Verma, national spokesperson of the BJP, is live with me.
Rahul Singh is a spokesperson of the Congress.
And Rajat Sethi, political analyst.
We have Ravesha Pradeep, who is the CJP spokesperson.
I'm going to begin with you, Ms.
Verma.
Why this unprecedented deployment in the national capital?
I was there on the ground.
I have not seen something even close to what I witnessed today.
It was similar to lockdown that we saw during the COVID times.
You know, Maria, thank you for having me over.
So the first point is this.
Under Article 254 of the Constitution, Article 246,
Entry one, entry two, entry four, list one, seventh schedule of the Indian Constitution.
Law and order is the prerogative of the government of the day, the Modi government in this case.
So if the Modi government has done the needful to ensure that the law and order machinery works seamlessly, I don't think anybody should be having any problems.
Point number two, what happened on the 20th of July at Jantar Mantar?
These are slogans that were raised and social media is full of such incendiary slogans.
And what was the response of the Cockroach Janta Party leaders, Sourav Das, Abhijit Dipken, Ashutosh Ranka?
These are not our people and there can't be a ban on freedom of speech.

the entire cockroach gang maria keeps talking about article 19 has given us the right to protest excuse me the same article 19 also says that no fundamental right is absolute it is subject to reasonable restrictions pertaining to public order morality and final point is this maria my final point

Has anybody from the Cockroach Janata Party, has Rahul Gandhi, has Priyanka Vadra, has Mamata Banerjee, has Akhilesh Yadav, has anybody once spoken out against the violence that was unleashed against ACP of Punjabi Bagh?
against the ACP of Connacht Place, against the Special Commissioner, Mr. Anishina.
In fact, I have spoken to a number of them, and all of them have condemned it.
So I'm going to move ahead, and I will ask Ravesha Pradeep, CJP National Spokesperson, first now to respond to this.
Ravesha, if you look at the Delhi Police's
rational tweet which was put out yesterday, they said that because the protest turned violent on 20th of July, this is precautionary measure which is being taken today.
How does the CJP look at developments of today, particularly that their leadership was picked up from inside the aircraft?
Right, right.
So thank you for having me on the panel tonight.
So having said that, I feel like this way of preventive detention of potential protesters is extremely unlawful.
And having said that, there is also a selective way of detaining people on ground.
For example,

You are completely letting the RSS goons go berserk on peaceful protesters on ground and you are completely watching the show, the Delhi police is watching the show while these goons are completely going crazy over peaceful protesters on ground.
And when you are talking about trying to maintain harmony or trying to detain people because you don't want things to go out of hand.
So I don't understand this nitpicking of whom you want to detain and whom you do not want to detain.
And another point I want to bring out is

When the national capital is unfortunately infamous for a lot of crimes that happen against women, then you don't see this kind of preventive measures or any measures taken by the Delhi police to curb it.
But now when you see them, there is a huge battalion that has come out to pick up Ashutosh, to pick up Saurabh and Deepak.

So, you know, this way of, you know, acting so promptly, I mean, I'm surprised to know that this is actually possible in Delhi, you know, because for years we thought that maybe this is not how the police... It's the national capital.
It is the national capital.
Yeshwar Dhanazad, you have been a cop for decades, now retired.
Tell me when was the last time private citizens were picked up from inside an aircraft?
Well, that was not really required.
I understand they could have easily been picked up in a more decent manner.
And in fact, they could have been picked up in Bombay because in Bombay also everywhere there were arrests going on.
I think what has happened is absolutely unprecedented.

And I think it is because that, as I always maintain, that the institutions, when they lose credibility, I'll just give you an example that three years back in London, the Metropolitan Police Commissioner, Mark Rowley,
Against the wishes of the home minister and even Rishi Sunak, he allowed a pro-Palestinian march.
And he said that the threat does not cross the threshold, which will be a danger to public safety or public order.
Here, if the police commissioner also exercised his authority,
He could have easily managed a crowd of 8 to 10,000 people as a protest.
And the only thing was that it was important for the police commissioner to stand up and say, no, I can manage this.
And he could have given them a protest side.
At least there would have been a negotiating contract that you come, fine, I give you this area, you'll be here for six hours.
And you will not vandalize or do anything.
Otherwise, we are going to take strong action.
And this would have put the cockroach party on the defensive.
And if they would have done something with the body cams and all that, the police, not the police, the government would have had an upper hand.
But, unfortunately, by not negotiating, not doing... I mean, these are technical things.
You know, there are instant protests all over the world.
Allow it.
How does it matter?
It doesn't really make a difference.
Some of them climb barricades.
Some of them, you know, jump here and there.
It really doesn't matter because democracy...
all this happened.
So it's an unfortunate incident and now what has happened is because there was no negotiations or anything, people have been detained.
I've been trying to see my friend's daughter who's been detained.
So this will lead to another call and this thing will keep on going on and on with no end.
So what was... Okay, so perhaps Sanju Verma should answer this.
Sanju Verma,
But, you know, Delhi police can have this kind of deployment for one day or maybe a couple of days.
It can come up with this rationale once, twice.
What happens if they give another call for protest?
Will Delhi be shut down again?
You know, Maria, let's get one thing very, very clear.
Institutions have not lost their credibility.
I beg to disagree with Mr. Azhar.
There is an attempt to delegitimize the Delhi police.
There is an attempt to delegitimize the Office of the Prime Minister.
There is an attempt to delegitimize the Office of the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah.
There is an attempt to brazenly delegitimize the Office of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Wherefore, the last time private citizens were picked off a flight, a plane you asked, and a ballot question.

When was the last time you saw the BJP saying TN Seshant was a thief, SY Qureshi is a thief, Ashok Lavasa is a thief, OP Rawat Ji is a thief, Nagendra Singh was a thief because he was CEC under Congress, RK Trivedi was a thief because he was CEC under Congress, MS Gil was a thief because he was CEC under Congress,
There can be disagreements.
We have never bravely maligned the Constitutional Office of the Chief Election Commissioner.
We lost one election after another.
We lost Karnataka.
We did not blame the Election Commission.
We lost Himachal.
We lost Kerala.
We lost Tamil Nadu.
We lost Telangana.
We went back to the drawing board.
But what does Rahul Gandhi do?
What does Priyanka Vadra do?
What does Mamata Banerjee do?
Mamata Banerjee ruled for 15 long years.
The moment she's thrown.

Rahul, this is all being done by the Congress party and other India blog because you are not able to connect with the people and because you are not able to connect with the people you are trying to mobilize the same people that you have not been able to connect and hold these protests.
and you are raising this entire issue repeatedly against the CEC and the election commission in particular because you are losing elections.
That's the charge not once but multiple times by the BJP.
Maya, but the issue today is what happened today is not just unprecedented or unfortunate.
It was also an equivocal announcement of emergency in India.
How many times
Do we see three former chief ministers, dozens of members of Parliament, more than 3,000 students and young protesters getting picked up in the national capital of the country?
Forty thousand policemen were on duty today, and they converted the entire central Delhi into a police garrison.
My fellow spokesperson from the Bharat Janta Party talked about right to freedom, fundamental rights of people.
100 trains were cancelled.
57 metro stations were shut down.
Entire central Delhi was brought to halt.
Patients couldn't reach hospitals.
Students couldn't reach colleges and schools.
People couldn't reach their offices.
Is right to free movement not a fundamental right?
Was this fundamental right not breached?
Maria, one other thing, one other very severe thing happened today.
Police entered Bangla Sahib Gurdwara.
How many times do we see incidents like this?
And when a young activist called the Manjeet Kaur raised the issue, she was threatened with NSA.
She was threatened with NSA because she comes from a minority background, and it was done by people like my fellow spokesperson, Sanjuji, by the BJP IT cell.
This entire protest is not
just raised by the Indian National Congress.
Yes, this issue was first talked about by the Indian National Congress, but this has now become a national issue because 13 crore people lost their right to vote.

You know, another important point that has been made by Sanju Verma with regards to election commission should be responded by the former CEC, and then I'll bring in Rajat Sethi for his opening comments.
OP Rawat,
Did the BJP, because help us remind our viewers, did the BJP discredit the election commission institution as much as the India block is doing?
What really happened?
Actually, it is in the realms of politics, and one cannot attempt a comparison.
But every time, anybody losing names the referee the election commission.
Only thing is that it's not really fair because the referee doesn't help anyone to win or doesn't affect the chances of others and they lose.
Referee is there to deliver free, fair, and credible election.
And this has been done by Election Commission of India as certified by Honorable Supreme Court in 2017 that although the parliament has not enacted any law for their selection,
We are satisfied that all those who are appointed as CEC and EC till now, they ensure delivery of free, fair, and credible election continuously.
But Mr. Rawat, has India witnessed these kind of protests against CEC in the past as well?
I know about political protests, I know about BJP holding protests when they were in opposition, but a protest by pressure group and the scale of these protests?
Never before, never before.
In fact, once
Aam Aadmi party brought out a very small procession and election commission came out and met them at the gate.
That was over.
So the CEC in this case also can walk an extra mile and ensure that he meets the 300 MPs that Rahul Gandhi says want to hold a meeting with the CEC and the election commissioners.

You said it, anyone, any stakeholders seeking a meeting with the election commission must be welcomed immediately and immediately heard and resolve the issues, the doubts they're having and everything will be sorted out.
So that's what former CEC is saying.
Sanju Verma, you wanted to come in.
Maria, very quickly, I first want to say this to the Congress spokesperson.
There is a video that is viral on social media.
Rahul Gandhi has both his hands like this on a female police constable.
And there is another video where Priyanka Vadra with her elbow is shoving it hard into the stomach of a female police constable.
So Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Vadra have no business giving basha on political propriety, ethics or morality.
And to Mr. Rawat, I will just say one thing.
All right.
All right.
We'll try and connect with Sanju Verma.
Let me bring in Rajat Sethi.
Rajat, I appreciate your patience on the show.
Rajat, you know, as a journalist who was on ground zero covering this protest, I also saw a number of citizens being inconvenienced.
You know, I have not, the last time we saw shut down of Connaught Place was during the COVID times.
You have a situation when the Delhi police says that India is the fastest growing economy and then the business district in Connaught Place, the offices, the shops and the restaurants are shut.
So, Maraji, we'll have to contextualize the protest and how should a police of a metropolitan city behave.
We'll have to pick certain examples from the other cosmopolitan like Washington, D.C.
Can you organize a protest of the scale around the White House itself, for instance?
What happens if you do it around the Capitol itself?
Or try out France.
There are areas perhaps which are designated, and we also know that if the spillover happens, how brutally the police cracks down on that.
That is also a case.
Here as well, while we can all debate this,
The inconvenience point that was brought out, you've seen when you allow protests to happen, a Shaheen Bagh is created.
Lacks of people for seven, eight months were inconvenienced.
We don't account for that.

When the key highways which were connecting Delhi to important states like UP, Himachal and all were choked by the farmers during the farmer protest, then also nobody wants to account for the citizens'
issues about commuting between Delhi and outside.
I mean, see, this is where I think fundamentally we have to go deeper into the issue and have civic engagements and understand where, how should the police deal with it.
If today, you know, there was stone pelting issues which were recorded on the cameras.
The body cam immediately released those videos through official channels of police saying that this is what happens now if we crack down on them.
then you will give us bad press.
If we allow that to happen and if some untoward incident happens there, what is the repercussions?
Who's going to take that responsibility?
Then you will point the gun again at the political leadership of the police.
So police also is in a fix.
It's not like they love doing this.
You need to give more practical answers and more practical suggestions from both the sides.
But my problem is that that platform does not exist.
The CJP spokesperson right now, the way she started, she's like RSS goons.
If I start saying this cockroach goon, if I start addressing her with this way, would she like it?
a person who's not here or an organization whose spokesperson is not here, can you start out by attributing such malicious words around an organization?
Is this fair?
Is this legal?
Is this right?

So my point is that you can see, can we have a civilized window where in all, as all the stakeholders can come together and identify ways that, okay, we will not hide behind the fact, disown certain elements who are the rowdy elements and want to create trouble.
You cannot come out and say, oh, hey, we were cool.
We were protesting calmly.
But there are some of these anti-social elements who created disturbance.
You'll have to own it entirely.
If you can own it entirely along with the repercussions which come with it, tomorrow you cannot go out and say that I'll march inside the parliament because that's a no-go zone.
You cannot say that tomorrow I'm going to just march inside the prime minister's house.
That is not allowed.
Create your own boundaries.
I'll ask Rahul and Ravesha to respond to this, the points that have been made by Rajat.
Ravesha, please come in.
Yes, yes.
So, Rajat, you need to understand that we are not protest fanatics, right?
Protesting is, if anything, the most ultimate choice that a citizen has in this country.
If anything, we also want the government to come forward, the ECI to come and have a dialogue and discussion.
We are completely in accordance with what you're saying, you know.
So coming on the streets and protesting is absolutely no joy for anybody.
So we come back to the main question.
Whatever we're discussing right now is completely secondary.
The primary question is,
When the government wants to respond, why is it usually by deploying police forces, barricading, shutting down Delhi?
Why are these the mechanisms to respond?
Why are you not trying to intervene and have a dialogue discussion with public?
So when you are not willing to do that, then everything that you're saying otherwise is just extremely illogical.
What will be a dialogue?
What is extremely illogical Maria?
If I may ask you, allow me to step in here.
I will tell you.
One incident happened in June, July, where in the police themselves went ahead, Suwamoto gave them the permission.
How was that permission abused?
Do you want to make that into a law that now our job of application is over?
Only then you will respond, only then you will probably react to it.
Why should the citizens come down on streets and protest for enormous days and then subsequently is when we are heard?
That is not how our democracy is.
No, one thing, Ravesha, here the protests are
protestors are demanding resignation of a constitutional body, someone who is holding an office, there has to be, you know, he cannot be removed, there is a process of impeachment.
So you know, it's not the same as demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan and then he went ahead and resigned on 25th, you know, five days after the protest turned violent.
So there are these very different authorities that we are looking at here.
And that's why I'll bring in Rajat.
Yes, Ravesha, go ahead.
Sorry.
Go ahead.
Ravesha, go ahead.
Yes, yes.
So I understand that it's not exactly as synonymous as we look at the education minister's resignation.
It's not that.
And I'm cognizant of that.
But all I'm trying to say is there is a problem.
There is an accusation that has been made.
And why is the CEC not trying to intervene?
The former CEC TN station, when he was wrongly addressed as the CEC of the government of India, he immediately barged in and he told reporters that, no, I am not the CEC of the government of India.
I am the CEC of India.
So something that, you know,
usually looks so minor has been corrected immediately.
Now, Gyanesh has been accused of so many misconducts and we don't hear him try to clean the whole image that is, you know.
So he should perhaps address a press conference and a lot of things will get answered then.
Rajat.
Why is he not doing this?
And the discussion of vote-chori has been long started.
One moment, Sanju Verma.
Rajat, go ahead.
So again, my simple point is that
a constitutional body.
How does the constitutional body come out?
What should be that mode of engagement?
Because tomorrow you can talk about a chief justice also or a justice of the Supreme Court and say that, hey, I don't like his judgment.
Let us drag him to the streets.
And let us deliver, deliver the justice as we wish on the streets.
Let us be the judge, jury and executioner on all issues, including of constitutional bodies.
Where have you established there is an active case going on?
The hearings are going on in the Supreme Court on this very issue.
Can't you have the patience for a week's time to understand how that goes ahead?
Can there be patience?
Who else is the arbiter on this issue?
Who is the arbiter?
Yes.
Okay.
Rahul.
Maria, Sanjuji talked about certain pictures of Rahul and Pranka Gandhi.
Why were Rahul and Pranka Gandhi put into that position?
I'll tell you why.
Elected MPs were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar.
Elected MPs were stopped from meeting the Election Commissioner of India.
Elected MPs were stopped
from going to Rajahat and peacefully doing the Satyagraha and all of this was done by Amit Shah's police.
Amit Shah's police illegally detained female MPs and I'll tell you why that happened illegally.
Those detentions happened after eight o'clock when after six o'clock it is illegal to detain any woman.
Why was Priyanka Gandhi wardrobe?
Why was Mawa Moitra and other members of parliament and workers of the opposition parties detained after sunset?
Is that legal?
Why has the Delhi Police or the Home Ministry not issued any statement on any of this?
Sanjeev Sharma, quick response on that and then I'll bring in Yashwardhan Azad and OP Rawat and wrap up this discussion.
Please go ahead.
Maria, let's get one thing very, very clear.
Law and order is the preserve of the government.
And what has been the attitude of Abhijit Dipke?
He tells Amit Shah, you are heading Delhi police, which is a bunch of criminals.
Priyanka Vadra says, Delhi police is a bunch of molesters.
CEC is a constitutional position under Article 324.
Has Gyanesh Kumar violated Article 326?
No.
Has Gyanesh Kumar violated Rule 13 and 16 of the Registration of Electoral Rules, 1916?
No.
Has Gyanesh Kumar violated Section 21 of the Representation of People Act?
No.
Is SIR a valid, legal, democratic exercise?
But Sanjay Verma, Gyanesh Kumar himself can respond to all that and say that there has been no violation at all.
I'm coming to that.
I'm coming to that.
Maria, that's a very nice question.
Why is BJP defending the CEC?
Why is BJP defending Gyanesh Kumar?
I have been asked this a zillion times on your widely watched show.
Let me say this.
What have the cockroaches been saying?
Ravisha is nodding her head.
Yes, they have been saying it.
Gyanu is not your friend.
Gyanu is a constitutional position holder.
I say Abhijit Duttke is worthy of winning the society election.
Saurabh Das is worthy of winning the society election.
Sanju ji, wait.
Is he worthy of winning the society election?
Is he worthy?
Yashwardhan Azad and OP Rawat on the screen now please.
OP Rawat, the point that has been made by the CJP national spokesperson with regards to what TN session was spoken about and how he immediately corrected it.
Do you think
As we have been saying it repeatedly, the time has come for the election commission themselves to come out and defend themselves, correct the perception, answer those questions that are being raised.
Otherwise, these protests are not stopping and even as we speak, in fact, fresh round of call for protests have been given by the CJP.
Actually, Maria, this snowballing of the whole thing is because they did not come out in open through media to public.

On every issue, internal dissensions as well as illegalities committed in SIR, like 93% eligible voters were deleted, could not vote in West Bengal election, and now they are found eligible voters by the appellate tribunal.
All these things need to be addressed by Election Commission squarely so that all of the India knows what is what.
And I think everything will be fizzling out.
So if the Election Commission addresses those questions, then it will fizzle out, is the sense that is coming in from the former CEC.
Yashwada Nazat, come in now.
With regards to deployment, lots of questions.
These were precautionary.
And as Rajat said, that perhaps
We can look at model of similar deployments which have happened in Washington or others if they are called for protests.
How do these equations or examples work?
No, no, let's first talk about the CC himself.

When thousands of people are on the streets, when CC has provenly done wrong, when Supreme Court has said that they did not give any carte blanche on Form 6, and when everyone has almost joined, including the ex-CC, including the ex-Supreme Court judges, this is democracy.

Whether he has a constitutional post or any post, yes, if there's a chief justice against... But Mr. Azad, there are a number of former judges who have also come out in support of Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commission.
True.
There will be a division in the society.
So, where does the right to protest disappear?
That's exactly what I'm saying.
If there's a large chunk of people, they have a right to protest.
And why I'm talking about institutional credibility is, let the police commissioner be absolutely independent.
He'll say, yes, I can manage a crowd of 10,000 people.
That is no problem.
Just leave it to me.
So, obviously, yes, when people say that it's the government which is in charge of law and order, government is responsible.
But the person who executes this is the police commissioner.
It's unfortunate that this thing has come to this pass, that today, for every opposition, the police is brutal.
For every government,
The police is absolutely all right.
But where is the question of police reforms?
Nobody talks about it.
Supreme Court reforms are not being implemented.
The government is also not implementing.
The Model Police Act is not being—and the opposition is also not saying that there should be police reforms.
And last point.
Yes, I agree with Mr. Sethi when he says there has to be something on protest management.
which where it is to be done, how many people, how many days, there has to be some negotiation on this point.
I wish the police commissioner had done it, but unfortunately he's taken the orders right from the top without even questioning.
Okay, so let's start wrapping it up with last comments from all the political guests who are there on the show.
I'm going to begin with Ravesha Pradeep of the CJP.
I'm extremely happy that few of the panelists here have really covered a lot of things that I wanted to say.

And yes, I think when we're talking about detention and about controlling the crowd, you largely have to see what are the roots and what is the space and you know, of course monitor if there are any anti national activities that are probably happening right, but you cannot
You cannot catch hold of any person you see on the streets and drag them and put them in buses and subsequently where we cannot even trace their whereabouts.
And when questioned of that, where are you getting these orders from?
They say orders, so these kind of blatant butchering of democracy is something that we will not be OK with.
Sanju and Rahul, quick 30 seconds to both of you, please.
Sanju, please go ahead.
In fact, I'll give you the last word, ma'am.
One moment.
Let Rahul speak for 30 seconds.
Yeah.
Maria, I'll end with a few questions.
Question number one, we are going to continue with the protest.
Is the police going to continue with the kind of provisions that were put into place today?
Question number two, Sandhuji very conveniently did not answer about the illegal detention of female MPs of the opposition parties.
She has to and Amit Shah's police has to answer those questions.
Question number three,
I'll just quickly, in 10 seconds, Gurdwara Sahib's entity was violated today.
Why are they not speaking up on that?
Quickly ma'am, Sanju Verma, 30 seconds.
Let's wrap this up, please.
Yes.
So Maria, let me just say through your show.
Hats off to Demi Police.
Hats off to the Chief Election Commissioner.
Despite being abused, he has shown class and restraint.
Hats off to the ordinary citizens of this country.

When Abhijit Titke was saying Inkalab Zindabad, the ordinary citizen said... Alright, thank you so much for joining me on the show tonight, Rishabh Vardhan Azad, Sanju Verma, OP Rawat, Rahul, Rajat and Ravisha.
Let's move on to what really played out politically as well.
